\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Discrete derivative]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p222-b004
}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.setCoordinate}
For a nonnegative integer $n$ and a coordinate $i$, the discrete derivative in
coordinate $i$ is the linear operator on real-valued functions on $\{-1,1\}^n$ that
sends $f$ to the function whose value at $x$ is $\bigl(f(x^{i,+})-f(x^{i,-})\bigr)/2$,
where $x^{i,+}$ and $x^{i,-}$ are obtained by setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $1$ and
$-1$, respectively.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
and let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on that cube. The discrete derivative in
coordinate $i$ of $f+g$ equals the sum of the discrete derivatives of $f$ and $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of the discrete derivative]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_smul}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_smul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $c$ be a real number, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on that cube. The
discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ of $c f$ equals $c$ times the discrete derivative
of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
and let $f$ be a real-valued function on that cube. For every point $x$ and every sign
$b$, the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at the point obtained by setting
coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $b$ equals its value at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb
R$. The discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$, given at $x$ by half the
difference between the values of $f$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and to $-1$, depends
only on coordinates $j\ne i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero discrete derivative criterion]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_ne_zero_iff}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_ne_zero_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
and let $f$ be a real-valued function on that cube. For every point $x$ of the cube, the
discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at $x$ is nonzero if and only if the values
of $f$ at the two points obtained from $x$ by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and to $-1$
are unequal.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate of the $n$-dimensional sign cube,
let $S$ be a set of coordinates, and let $x$ be a point of the cube. The discrete
derivative in coordinate $i$ of the sign monomial indexed by $S$, evaluated at $x$,
equals the monomial indexed by $S\setminus\{i\}$ if $i\in S$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, and let $i$ be one of its coordinates. At every point $x$ of the cube, the
discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ is $\displaystyle
\sum_{S\subseteq[n]:\,i\in S}\widehat f(S)\,\chi_{S\setminus\{i\}}(x)$, where $\widehat
f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_T$ is the sign monomial
indexed by $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Pivotal indicator]
\lean{FABL.pivotalIndicator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b003}
\label{FABL.pivotalIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPivotal}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, taking values in
$\{\pm1\}$. For a coordinate $i$ and sign vector $x$, the pivotal indicator is $1$ if
flipping coordinate $i$ changes $f(x)$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ to
$\{-1,1\}$, and choose a coordinate $i$ and a point $x$ in the cube. The square of the
discrete derivative of the real-valued version of $f$ at $x$ equals $1$ if flipping
coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Influence]
\lean{FABL.influence}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p046-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p265-b002
}
\statementsource{mossel-neeman-gaussian-noise-stability}{pdf-b53c1a5aa27d-p007-b003}
\label{FABL.influence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.discreteDerivative}
For a real-valued function $f$ on the sign cube of dimension $n$ and a coordinate $i$,
the influence of coordinate $i$ is the uniform expectation over $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ of the
square of the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of influence]
\lean{FABL.influence_nonneg}
\label{FABL.influence_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.influence}
\difficulty{3}
For every real-valued function $f$ on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and every coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the influence of $f$ at $i$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a
coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The influence of $f$ at $i$, the uniform average of
the squared discrete derivative in that coordinate, is positive if and only if that
derivative is nonzero at some point of the cube.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean
function, and let $i$ be a coordinate. The probability that flipping coordinate $i$
changes $f$ equals the average squared discrete derivative of the real-valued sign
representation of $f$ in coordinate $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Relevant coordinates]
\lean{FABL.IsRelevant}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b005}
\label{FABL.IsRelevant}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.influence}
For a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, call
$i$ relevant when its influence on $f$ is strictly positive.
\end{definition}

Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and let $i$ be a coordinate. The influence of $f$ at
$i$ is positive if and only if there is a sign-cube point $x$ such that the values of
$f$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and to $-1$ differ.
\end{theorem}

}
\label{FABL.coordinateExpectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.setCoordinate}
For a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and a coordinate $i$, define its coordinate
expectation by averaging the two values obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and to
$-1$, while leaving all other coordinates fixed. This operation is linear in $f$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and choose $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The coordinate expectation of $f$ at $x$ is the average of the two
values obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and to $-1$, respectively, while
leaving every other coordinate unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate in $	ext{Fin }n$, let $S$ be a set
of coordinates, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The average of the monomial indexed by $S$
over the two choices of the $i$th coordinate is $0$ if $i\in S$, and is the monomial's
value at $x$ if $i\notin S$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and choose $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The coordinate expectation of $f$ at $x$ is
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ i\notin S}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\widehat
f(S)$ is the uniform-cube Fourier coefficient and $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{j\in S}x_j$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $i$ be a coordinate in $\text{Fin }n$, let
$f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. For every sign $b\in\{−1,1\}$, the
average of $f$ over the two possible values of coordinate $i$ is unchanged when
coordinate $i$ of $x$ is replaced by $b$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, choose a coordinate
$i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Then $f(x)$ is the sum of $x_i$ times
the half-difference of the values of $f$ with coordinate $i$ set to $1$ and $-1$, and
the average of those two values.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate Laplacian]
\lean{FABL.coordinateLaplacian}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b005
}
\label{FABL.coordinateLaplacian}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coordinateExpectation}
For a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and a coordinate $i$, define the coordinate
Laplacian as $f$ minus its coordinate expectation at $i$.
\end{definition}

  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p049-b003}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let
$i$ be a coordinate, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates. The Fourier coefficient at $S$
of the function obtained by subtracting the average over the two possible values of
coordinate $i$ from $f$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ if $i\in S$, and
equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The influence of $f$ at
coordinate $i$ is the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over all subsets
containing $i$: $\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ i\in
S}\widehat f(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone with
respect to the coordinatewise orders. For every coordinate $i$ and every point $x$ in

at $x$ equals that derivative.

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p047-b006}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its influence
at coordinate $i$ equals its Fourier coefficient on the singleton set $\{i\}$:
$\operatorname{Inf}_i(f)=\widehat f(\{i\})$.
\end{theorem}
